comment: The site demo video's storyboard: positions and durations, never titles. Compiled by tools/site_video.py (`compile_storyboard`) to the dump driver's key schedule. Virtual time only advances on clean frames, so a duration is a duration of the FILM, and `gates` fails any beat whose picture was still visibly moving 0.2 s before the next beat's key (`gate_beats_at_rest`, on decoded frames). The film is shot with the hold hint taught (`plxnative-hintoff`, armed by `site_video.py render --storyboard`, recorded as `hold_hint: suppressed` in render.json): the capsule is a one-time teaching overlay and a film has no viewer to teach, so a rest on a card is as long as it reads calm. The profile chip is on the route up to the tab bar (up from the hero lands on it), so the harness signs the simulator in to the mock's Demo account and the chip reads Demo, never Sign in. The hero pages: `right` on the Info button turns the carousel forward and `left` on the Continue button turns it back (the app's own edge rule), so the film turns to the second page and back to the first before it goes down to the shelf. OK on the shelf's third card opens that title's Detail (the default Continue Watching press opens details; the no-playback gate proves nothing played). `down` there scrolls the page to its Cast & Crew row, where the catalog's `people` gives every performer of that title a portrait, and four more `down`s run through the rest of the page to its foot: the title's collection (its linked heading, then its shelf), More Like This, and the About section, where the film rests. Arrows only: nothing on the page is opened (a portrait's or a card's OK is another page, the About card's a reader), so a miscounted press changes where the page rests and nothing else, and `back` leaves the Detail from wherever it is scrolled. Keys that belong to one gesture share a beat, pressed `gap_ms` apart without waiting for rest: the rest gate judges a beat's END, and a remote pressed faster than the springs settle is what the film is there to show. The Movies page is walked with arrows only, never OK, so no count of presses can open a title, a collection or a menu there: six `down`s run from Continue Watching through Recently Added and the two collection shelves (each under its linked heading, a stop of its own) to the All heading's Type chip; `right` `right` to Filter, `down` into the poster grid's third column and three more moves inside columns 2 to 4 (never the sixth column, whose `right` is the letter rail; with the catalog's title order no card on that route is flagged `not_in_video`). The page is left the way it was entered: as many `up`s as there were `down`s (eight) walk back to the first shelf, where the page is at its top and one `back` returns Home. A `back` pressed lower down jumps the page to its top first, and that jump is NOT filmed: the first Linux render of it wrote different frames under the hold-injection gate (104 frames, from the press to the end of the return), so it is not yet a motion the dump can vouch for. Loop: the last frame is the first frame's composition (Home, hero, focus on Continue); `end.match_first_frame` is read by `gates` (`storyboard/loop`): the last frame may differ from the first by at most 1/255 in a channel.
